request.spec:
A claim that is moved to another person now receives the next number in the sequence it would be
numbered in (the sheet's, or its period's when per-period numbering is on), and its old number is
never used again; a draft, having no number, gets none. CLAIM_REASSIGNED carries the new number.
Moving claims together follows the same rule, in list order.

agent.result_text:
A claim moved to another person now gets a new number, and all 4 tests in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts` pass under `bin/e2e`.

The whole change is in `reassign` in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/claim/ClaimService.java`:

- **New number:** a moved claim that has a number takes the next one in its sequence. That's the sheet's sequence, or its period's when per-period numbering is on. Numbering follows the same rules as opening a claim.
- **Old number not reused:** under per-period numbering, the old number is added to the existing table of retired numbers so it is never given out again. The sheet-wide counter only ever goes up, so its numbers can't repeat anyway.
- **Drafts:** a draft has no number and still gets none when moved.
- **Audit:** `CLAIM_REASSIGNED` now carries the new number, because it already logs whatever number the claim has once it's saved.
- **Moving several at once:** this already processed claims in list order, one at a time through the same method, so it follows the same rule without changes.
- **Locking:** a move now locks the sheet for numbering before reading the claim, as opening a claim does, so two changes at the same moment can't take the same number.

I also updated the comment above `reassign`, which said a moved claim keeps its number. Nothing else changed: no database, front-end or screen changes were needed.
